title: Keep your business and income running
seoTitle: Business continuity when moving abroad | EXOBASIS
description: Prepare your owner-dependent business for departure or absence: authorised people, payments, customer work, access and the obligations that continue abroad.
intro:
If your business depends on you, leaving the country can become a choice between protecting your family and keeping your income. The practical answer is to make the essential work continue while you travel, are unavailable or establish a new base.

A business continuity plan for a small business starts with the decisions, payments and customer commitments that only you can handle today. Then it gives somebody else the authority, information and working access to carry them through.

primary.label: Prepare my business for departure or absence

knowledgeSummary.title: Keep your business running when you need to leave
facts: Identify the work that cannot wait for the owner.
Give suitable people accepted powers and named access.
Test essential tasks before the real absence.
knowledgeSummary.imageAlt: Notebook and pen, symbolising organised preparation.

sections.title: Find the work that would stop without you
sections.body:
Take a normal trading week and identify what would fail if you could not answer. Include payroll, supplier payments, client delivery, approvals, invoicing, collections and statutory deadlines. Rank the work by the consequence of delay, not by how often you normally do it.

An owner-absence plan in practical terms
TaskWhat the replacement needsEvidence it can continue
Pay staff and essential suppliersApproved payment authority, available funds and the payment calendar.An authorised payment can be prepared and approved through the agreed process.
Deliver work to a clientCurrent scope, files, next milestone and an accountable contact.The substitute can locate the latest work and handle the next agreed step.
Issue and follow up invoicesCorrect entity, tax details, customer records and billing access.A test invoice can be prepared correctly without using your personal login.
Meet a filing or renewal deadlineThe date, responsible adviser, records and required signatory.The adviser knows who can supply information and give instructions.

Use the results to remove the most serious single-person dependencies first. A detailed handbook is useful only when the named people can perform the work it describes.

sections.title: Keep clients, delivery and invoicing connected
sections.body:
Give each active engagement a short handover: what was sold, what has been delivered, the next commitment, the current files and who can decide a change. Make the customer-facing contact a managed business channel rather than a personal number that disappears with your SIM.

If you expect disruption, agree who communicates with clients and what they can commit to. A replacement should be able to explain the next delivery step, record an issue and escalate a decision without improvising the contract.

Keep invoicing and collections on the same operating plan. Confirm the billing entity and bank details, protect changes to payment instructions with a verification process, and assign responsibility for overdue invoices. Money arriving late can undermine both the business and the family’s move.

sections.title: Match the authority to the payment or decision
sections.body:
For every critical action, identify the person who may perform it and the basis of that authority. A company directorship, bank mandate, employment delegation and personal power of attorney serve different purposes. Sharing a password does not settle the right to approve a payment or sign for the company.

Ask the bank and key providers to confirm the accepted arrangement. Set appropriate payment limits, required approvals, substitute people and the procedure for revoking access. Provide named user access wherever the system supports it.

If you become unable to make decisions, the business may need a different authority chain from an ordinary holiday absence. Connect company governance, shareholder rights and personal representation through the powers of attorney and succession guide. The documents and the institution’s accepted process need to work together.
sections.after: Banking access and payments abroad→Powers of attorney, representation and succession abroad→

sections.title: Test access from somewhere other than your usual desk
sections.body:
Prepare a working device, an independent connection and recovery methods that remain available if your main phone or email fails. Keep business documents in an organised system with access assigned to the people who need them. Test restoring the files required for a real task, not just opening the backup application.

Run an owner-absence exercise. Let the substitute find the current client file, prepare an invoice, identify the payment approval and reach the adviser without asking you for a code. Use a safe test or low-risk authorised task, with the exercise agreed in advance. Record what prevented completion.

At the destination, test the workspace, connection, power arrangements, privacy and client-call hours. If access depends on your home-country phone number, establish a supported recovery or replacement route before changing that number.
sections.after: When your phone, SIM and main email fail→Set up private communications and recovery access→

sections.title: Resolve the rules for the work you will actually do abroad
sections.body:
Working from another country can change the legal and administrative questions even if your customers stay where they are. Set out where you will physically work, for whom, for how long and in what role. An employee needs a different assessment from a company director or self-employed consultant.

Confirm the destination permission for the intended activity, the employer’s agreement where relevant and the applicable payroll and social-insurance treatment. Give the adviser the itinerary, duties and employing entity, rather than asking only whether remote work is possible.

Keep these decisions alongside the family’s residence plan. A home suitable for living may still be unsuitable for the business activity, insurance conditions or client confidentiality requirements. Resolve those connections before committing to the location.

sections.title: Running a UK company from abroad: keep the company obligations visible
sections.body:
UK company directors do not have to live in the UK, but the company must have a UK registered office. Directors remain legally responsible for running the company and ensuring that accounts and reports are properly prepared. Appointing a company secretary does not remove that responsibility.

Source: GOV.UK: directors and company secretaries.

A director’s ability to live abroad does not answer the company’s cross-border tax position. Put the actual management decisions, contracts, work locations, staff and premises before the relevant tax advisers. Keep the personal departure assessment separate from the company assessment, then reconcile the results.

An overseas company is appropriate when its purpose, administration, banking and continuing costs fit the activity. If you need one, EXOBASIS can organise the formation and administration work with the relevant specialists. Moving a registration on paper while the business continues elsewhere does not describe where its activity actually takes place.

sections.title: Put the continuity arrangements into working order
sections.body:
EXOBASIS maps the owner-dependent tasks, organises the required specialist and institutional work, prepares the document and access arrangements, and coordinates the agreed absence exercise. We also arrange the destination workspace and the practical tasks that connect business continuity with your family’s move.

The handover identifies who can act, what they need, the steps actually tested and the remaining dependencies. You can commission a focused recovery-access or representation task, an overseas-company engagement or a connected family and business plan.

Start with the task you cannot afford to have stop. That gives us a concrete point from which to prepare the rest.
